title: NURS 1017 Unit 6 Case Study 7
description: 42-year-old female client with 8 months of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive symptoms, irritable bowel and headaches, diagnosed with fibromyalgia after normal tests; central sensitization, the pain–sleep cycle, suicide risk screening, self-management teaching, and evaluation at 3 months.

authorReview.note:
New case written by Claude on 14 Oct 2026 to fill a Unit 6 gap; please review before using it with students:
Screen 3–4: the case includes an indirect suicidal statement and the Canadian 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline; consider mentioning this to the class before using it.
Screen 2: the diagnostic criteria are described as in the ACR 2010/2016 criteria (tender points no longer required).

question.stem: Which findings are consistent with fibromyalgia? Select all that apply.

options.text: A hug or a tight waistband hurts
Works as a dental hygienist
Trouble concentrating and remembering
Takes a multivitamin daily
Wakes unrefreshed after 9 hours in bed
Heart rate 82 beats/min
Abdominal cramping with alternating diarrhea and constipation
Tension headaches 3 to 4 times a week
Blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg
Pain on both sides of the body, above and below the waist, for 8 months

question.explanation:
Consistent with fibromyalgia: chronic (3 months or more) widespread pain on both sides of the body and above and below the waist is the core feature. It is accompanied by unrefreshing sleep, fatigue, and cognitive symptoms (“fibro fog”). Pain from touch that should not hurt (allodynia, such as a hug or a waistband) reflects an oversensitive pain system. Other functional conditions are common alongside it: irritable bowel syndrome, tension headaches and migraines, temporomandibular disorder, and anxiety or depression.

Not cues: a multivitamin, a normal heart rate and blood pressure, and her job. Note also what is absent: no joint swelling, normal strength and range of motion, and no fever or weight loss. Fibromyalgia does not damage joints or muscles, and swelling, fever, weight loss or true muscle weakness would suggest another diagnosis.

question.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

cloze.text: The normal ESR, CRP, and CK show that the client's pain is not caused by [[drop0]]. Fibromyalgia is best explained by [[drop1]], in which [[drop2]]. Poor sleep [[drop3]].

options.text: the nervous system
inflammation or muscle damage
stress
an autoimmune attack on the joints
infection of the muscles
central sensitization
degeneration of the joint cartilage
the joints fill with inflammatory fluid
the brain and spinal cord amplify pain signals and dampen the body's own pain control
the muscles release enzymes that damage nerves
protects her muscles from injury
lowers the pain threshold and worsens fatigue
has no effect on her pain

question.explanation:
Normal tests: fibromyalgia is not an inflammatory, autoimmune or degenerative disease, and it does not damage muscles or joints. Normal ESR and CRP show no inflammation, a normal CK shows no muscle damage, and a negative RF and ANA make rheumatoid arthritis and lupus unlikely. A normal TSH rules out hypothyroidism, and normal hemoglobin and ferritin rule out anemia and iron deficiency as causes of the fatigue. The diagnosis is clinical (widespread pain for 3 months or more with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive symptoms, not better explained by another condition); tender-point counts are no longer required.

Central sensitization: the pain is real, but it comes from how the nervous system processes signals. Pain pathways in the spinal cord and brain become overactive (more excitatory neurotransmitters such as substance P and glutamate), while the descending pathways that normally dampen pain (serotonin, norepinephrine) are less active. Ordinary sensations are felt as painful (allodynia), and painful ones hurt more than they should (hyperalgesia). Stress affects the condition but is not the cause.

Sleep: people with fibromyalgia have less deep, restorative sleep. Poor sleep lowers the pain threshold and worsens fatigue and concentration, and more pain disturbs sleep further, creating a cycle that nursing care aims to break.

question.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

cloze.text: The nurse's priority concern is the client's risk for [[drop0]], as evidenced by [[drop1]]. Her long afternoon naps [[drop2]].

options.text: falls
acute pain
suicide
ineffective work performance
her pain rating of 8/10
the 6 missed workdays
her statement that everyone would be better off without her and her PHQ-9 score of 17
are needed to restore her energy
have no effect on her symptoms
worsen her night-time sleep and keep the pain–sleep cycle going

question.explanation:
Risk for suicide: “everyone would be better off without me” is an indirect statement of suicidal thinking. With a PHQ-9 of 17, social withdrawal, the loss of her relationship, and chronic pain (which on its own raises suicide risk), safety is the priority over pain, sleep or work concerns. The nurse never dismisses such a statement.

Pain, missed work and isolation are important and will be addressed, but they are not immediately life-threatening.

Daytime napping: long afternoon naps reduce the drive to sleep at night, which leads to short, unrefreshing night sleep; poor sleep then lowers the pain threshold. Short naps (under 30 minutes, early afternoon) or none are better.

question.stem: For each nursing action, click to specify whether it is indicated, contraindicated, or nonessential for the client at this visit.

rows.text: Ask the client directly whether she is thinking about ending her life and whether she has a plan
Promise to keep her suicidal thoughts a secret if she asks
Report her statement and PHQ-9 score to the provider before she leaves the clinic
Tell her that everyone feels this way sometimes and it will pass
Give her the 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline number (call or text)
Repeat the ESR and CRP today
Stay with her, or make sure someone stays with her, until the assessment is complete

question.explanation:
Indicated: asking directly about suicidal thoughts, a plan and the means does not plant the idea; it opens the conversation and is the only way to judge the level of risk. The provider must know before she leaves so that a safety plan and mental health follow-up are arranged. Canada's 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline is available 24/7 by phone or text. A client who may be at risk is not left alone until the risk has been assessed.

Contraindicated: the nurse cannot promise secrecy about a risk to the client's life; the information must be shared with the team. Saying “everyone feels this way” dismisses her distress and closes the conversation.

Nonessential: her inflammatory markers were normal and repeating them does not address her current risk.

question.stem: Which instructions should the nurse include in the client's self-management teaching? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pace yourself: break tasks into smaller parts and alternate activity with rest
Practise relaxation, such as slow breathing or mindfulness, to manage stress
Avoid caffeine after noon and screens for an hour before bed
Since your tests are normal, try to ignore the pain
Increase your coffee intake to fight the fatigue
Go to bed and get up at the same times every day, and limit naps
Avoid exercise until the pain improves
Do as much as you can on good days to catch up
Start with gentle aerobic exercise, such as walking or warm-water exercise, a few minutes at a time, and increase slowly

question.explanation:
Correct: regular aerobic exercise has the strongest evidence for reducing fibromyalgia pain and fatigue. It must start low and build slowly, because doing too much at once causes a flare. A regular sleep schedule, limited naps, and avoiding caffeine and screens before bed improve sleep quality (sleep hygiene). Pacing prevents the “boom-and-bust” pattern of overdoing it on good days and crashing afterward. Relaxation and stress management calm the overactive stress and pain systems.

Incorrect: avoiding exercise leads to deconditioning and more pain. Catching up on good days triggers flares. Extra caffeine disrupts sleep. Telling her to ignore the pain dismisses a real condition and damages trust; normal tests mean no tissue damage, not that the pain is imaginary.

question.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it indicates that the plan of care has been effective or not effective.

rows.text: “On good days I clean the whole house, and then I'm in bed for 2 days.”
Sleeps about 7 hours and wakes rested 4 nights a week
Drinks 5 cups of coffee a day, the last around 2000
PHQ-9 score 6; denies thoughts of self-harm
“I still don't see my friends; I never know how I'll feel.”

question.explanation:
Effective: less pain, better sleep, regular aerobic exercise, a return to work, and a much lower depression score with no suicidal thoughts show that the plan is working. Fibromyalgia is chronic; the goal is better function and quality of life, not a cure.

Not effective: the boom-and-bust pattern shows she is not yet pacing herself. Late, heavy caffeine intake undermines sleep. Avoiding friends increases isolation and the risk of depression. The nurse reinforces pacing and sleep hygiene, and explores ways to keep social contact (shorter visits, plans that can be changed).
